paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. In Christ, nobody is on the outside looking in anymore. Paul tells the Gentiles to remember they were once "without hope and without God in the world," and then comes that turn: "But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far away have been brought near through the blood of Christ." (Ephesians 2:12-13) That's not a small upgrade, that's a whole new address.

The reason it works is that Christ Himself is the peace. Paul says He "has made the two one and has torn down the dividing wall of hostility," and He did it to "create in Himself one new man out of the two." (Ephesians 2:14-15) Nobody had to climb over that wall or earn a way around it, because the cross put the hostility to death and "through Him we both have access to the Father by one Spirit." (Ephesians 2:16, 18) So if you've ever felt like the one who doesn't belong, hear me: the door is open, and Christ opened it.

And Paul doesn't stop at "welcome." He says you're "fellow citizens with the saints and members of God's household," part of a building with Christ Jesus Himself as the cornerstone. (Ephesians 2:19-20) So you don't hold one cookie by the door anymore, you've got a place in the house. Live like it, baker, because God is still building, and "in Him you too are being built together into a dwelling place for God in His Spirit." (Ephesians 2:22)
